title: Inspect and extend: Verify behavior and avoid overstating results
objective: Use the real implementation in `test/exposure.test.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve simulation tests, storage failures, labels, disclosure, and evidence limits.
problem: Tests can prove the model returns the expected simulation; they cannot prove a health service is present. Inspect assertions and visible disclaimers, then identify privacy and accessibility checks needed on-device. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `test/exposure.test.ts` and the related project files: test/exposure.test.ts; src/components.tsx; README.md.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to simulation tests, storage failures, labels, disclosure, and evidence limits.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: A passing unit suite does not validate clinical advice, health policy, or native exposure notifications.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: Tests can prove the model returns the expected simulation; they cannot prove a health service is present. Inspect assertions and visible disclaimers, then identify privacy and accessibility checks needed on-device.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `test/exposure.test.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Search for `empty history is labeled as unchecked` first.
Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
